item.title: Tracing Labeled Sulfur and Phosphorus into Macromolecules
item.stimulus:
Researchers grew two cultures of the same bacterium. Each culture's food source contained one radioactively labeled element. Cells use a radioactive form of an element in the same way as the ordinary form.

Culture 1: sulfur-35 (³⁵S)
Culture 2: phosphorus-32 (³²P)

After several generations, the cells from each culture were broken open and their molecules were separated into four fractions: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids. The radioactivity of each fraction was measured in counts per minute (cpm). Readings below 100 cpm are background and show that the label was not incorporated.

Fraction | Culture 1 (³⁵S), cpm | Culture 2 (³²P), cpm
Carbohydrates | 30 | 40
Lipids | 25 | 2100
Proteins | 8800 | 35
Nucleic acids | 20 | 6400

parts.prompt: Explain why the ³⁵S in Culture 1 was incorporated into the protein fraction.

criteria.text: Explains that sulfur is an element used in building proteins, so the cells built ³⁵S into the proteins they made.
criteria.evidence: Response states that sulfur is used to build proteins (is part of proteins) and connects this to the label appearing in the protein fraction.
criteria.fix: Memorize the element linked to each macromolecule: sulfur is used in building proteins, so a sulfur label marks protein.

parts.prompt: In Culture 2, ³²P was incorporated into two different fractions. Explain why each of these two fractions became labeled.

criteria.text: Explains that phosphorus is used in building nucleic acids, so ³²P was incorporated into the nucleic acid fraction (6400 cpm).
criteria.evidence: Response links the labeled nucleic acid fraction to phosphorus being an element used to build nucleic acids.
criteria.fix: Recall phosphorus is used in building nucleic acids; check that fraction first when a phosphorus label is used.

criteria.text: Explains that phosphorus is used in building phospholipids, a type of lipid, so ³²P was incorporated into the lipid fraction (2100 cpm).
criteria.evidence: Response links the labeled lipid fraction to phosphorus being an element used to build phospholipids.
criteria.fix: Recall phosphorus also builds phospholipids, which are lipids; a phosphorus label therefore appears in the lipid fraction too.

parts.prompt: Cellulose is a carbohydrate. A researcher grows cotton plants with ³²P in their water and then purifies cellulose from the cotton fibers. Predict whether the purified cellulose will contain ³²P, and justify your prediction.

criteria.text: Predicts that the purified cellulose will not contain ³²P (it will not be radioactive).
criteria.evidence: Response states the cellulose will not be labeled with ³²P.
criteria.fix: Decide whether the molecule class contains the labeled element; if not, predict no label in the purified molecule.

criteria.text: Justifies the prediction: carbohydrates such as cellulose are built from carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen and do not contain phosphorus.
criteria.evidence: Response states that carbohydrates are made of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen (no phosphorus), so phosphorus is not built into cellulose.
criteria.fix: Justify with elemental composition: carbohydrates are built of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen only, so they lack phosphorus.

item.model_answer:
(a) Sulfur is one of the elements used in building proteins. As the bacteria made new proteins, they used the ³⁵S from their food, so the label appeared in the protein fraction (8800 cpm), while the other fractions stayed at background.

(b) Phosphorus is used in building nucleic acids, so the cells built ³²P into their nucleic acids, labeling the nucleic acid fraction (6400 cpm).
Phosphorus is also used in building phospholipids, which are a type of lipid, so ³²P was built into phospholipids and the lipid fraction was labeled (2100 cpm).

(c) The purified cellulose will not contain ³²P. Cellulose is a carbohydrate, and carbohydrates are built from carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen; they do not contain phosphorus. This matches the data: the carbohydrate fraction in Culture 2 stayed at background (40 cpm).
item.verification_python:
c1={'carb':30,'lipid':25,'protein':8800,'nucleic':20}
c2={'carb':40,'lipid':2100,'protein':35,'nucleic':6400}
bg=100
lab1=sorted(k for k,v in c1.items() if not v<bg)
lab2=sorted(k for k,v in c2.items() if not v<bg)
assert lab1==['protein']
assert lab2==['lipid','nucleic']
assert len(lab2)==2
assert c2['carb']<bg
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Tracing Labeled Elements into Bacterial Macromolecules
item.stimulus:
Researchers grew three separate cultures of the bacterium Escherichia coli. Each medium contained all the nutrients needed for growth, but one nutrient in each culture carried a radioactive label. Culture 1 contained glucose labeled with carbon-14 (14C). Culture 2 contained phosphate labeled with phosphorus-32 (32P). Culture 3 contained sulfate labeled with sulfur-35 (35S). After several generations, the cells from each culture were broken open. Their macromolecules were separated into four fractions: proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and polysaccharides (carbohydrates). The researchers measured the percent of each culture's incorporated radioactivity found in each fraction.

Percent of incorporated radioactivity in each fraction
Label | Proteins | Nucleic acids | Lipids | Polysaccharides
14C | 55 | 20 | 10 | 15
32P | 0 | 82 | 18 | 0
35S | 100 | 0 | 0 | 0
item.model_answer:
(a) Carbon is one of the most prevalent elements in all biological macromolecules, including carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids. The cells used carbon atoms from the labeled glucose to build all four classes, so 14C appears in every fraction. Sulfur, however, is used only in building proteins, because some amino acids contain sulfur. Nucleic acids, lipids, and polysaccharides contain no sulfur, so all of the 35S ends up in the protein fraction.

(b) Counts in nucleic acids = 82% of 50,000 = 0.82 × 50,000 = 41,000 counts per minute.

(c) Once their stored phosphorus is used up, the cells will be unable to make new DNA or new plasma membrane, or will make far less of both. The 32P data show that phosphorus is incorporated only into nucleic acids (82%) and lipids (18%). Every DNA nucleotide contains a phosphate group, and the membrane bilayer is built from phospholipids, which also contain phosphorus. Atoms used to build new molecules must come from the environment, and glucose, sulfate, and nitrogen cannot supply phosphorus, so without phosphorus the cells cannot build these molecules.
item.verification_python:
from fractions import Fraction
rows={'C14':[55,20,10,15],'P32':[0,82,18,0],'S35':[100,0,0,0]}
for k,v in rows.items():
    assert sum(v)==100
assert all(x>0 for x in rows['C14'])
assert rows['S35'][0]==100
total=50000
nuc=Fraction(82,100)*total
assert nuc==41000
assert rows['P32'][1]+rows['P32'][2]==100
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Tracking Labeled Elements into Bacterial Macromolecules
item.stimulus:
Researchers investigated which elements bacteria use to build different macromolecules. They grew three identical cultures of the bacterium Escherichia coli for several generations. Each culture's medium contained one radioactively labeled source of an element:
Culture 1: glucose labeled with carbon-14 (14C)
Culture 2: phosphate labeled with phosphorus-32 (32P)
Culture 3: sulfate labeled with sulfur-35 (35S)
All other nutrients were unlabeled and present in excess. The cells were then collected and separated into four macromolecule fractions. The researchers measured the radioactivity in each fraction and expressed it as a percentage of the total label incorporated by that culture.

Percentage of incorporated label in each fraction
Fraction | 14C (Culture 1) | 32P (Culture 2) | 35S (Culture 3)
Protein | 52 | 2 | 96
Nucleic acid | 22 | 80 | 1
Phospholipid | 12 | 17 | 1
Polysaccharide | 14 | 1 | 2
Total | 100 | 100 | 100
item.model_answer:
(a) Phosphorus is required to build nucleic acids and phospholipids. In Culture 2, 80% of the incorporated 32P was in the nucleic acid fraction and 17% was in the phospholipid fraction, for a total of 97%, while only 2% was in protein and 1% in polysaccharide.

(b) Phospholipid fraction = 17% of total = 0.17 × 250,000 cpm = 42,500 cpm.

(c) Carbon, along with hydrogen and oxygen, is one of the most prevalent elements in all biological molecules; carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids are all built on carbon. Labeled carbon from glucose is therefore incorporated into every class of macromolecule. Phosphorus and sulfur, in contrast, are used to build only specific macromolecules: phosphorus in nucleic acids and phospholipids, and sulfur in proteins, so their labels are concentrated in those fractions.

(d) The cells will be most directly unable to synthesize new proteins. Sulfur is used in building proteins, as shown by 96% of the 35S label ending up in the protein fraction compared with only 1–2% in the other fractions. Without a sulfur source, the cells cannot build new protein, while nucleic acids and phospholipids can still be built from the available carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and phosphorus (nitrogen being supplied by the other nutrients).

assert p32[1]+p32[2]==97

assert s35[0]==96 and max(s35[1:])==2
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Tracking Radioactive Sulfur and Phosphorus Into Bacterial Macromolecules
item.stimulus:
A student investigated which elements bacteria use to build different macromolecules. Two cultures of the bacterium Escherichia coli were grown in identical nutrient media, except that each medium contained one radioactive isotope. Culture A received sulfate labeled with radioactive sulfur (³⁵S). Culture B received phosphate labeled with radioactive phosphorus (³²P). After several generations of growth, the cells were broken open. Their contents were separated into three fractions: proteins, nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), and phospholipids. The radioactivity in each fraction was measured and expressed as a percentage of the total radioactivity incorporated by that culture.

Percent of incorporated radioactivity in each fraction
Fraction | Culture A (³⁵S) | Culture B (³²P)
Proteins | 97 | 4
Nucleic acids | 2 | 78
Phospholipids | 1 | 18

Culture B incorporated a total of 50,000 counts per minute (cpm) of ³²P.
item.model_answer:
(a) Proteins contained most of the ³⁵S (97 percent). Sulfur is an element used to build proteins, because some amino acids contain sulfur. Nucleic acids and phospholipids are built mainly from C, H, O, N, and P and typically contain no sulfur, so very little ³⁵S appeared in those fractions.

(b) cpm in phospholipids = 0.18 × 50,000 cpm = 9,000 cpm.

(c) Phosphorus, in the form of phosphate, is used to build both types of molecule. Each nucleotide in DNA and RNA contains a phosphate group, and phospholipids also contain a phosphate group. The cells took up the labeled phosphate from the medium and built it into both nucleic acids and phospholipids, so both fractions were radioactive.

(d) I predict that all three fractions (proteins, nucleic acids, and phospholipids) will contain ¹⁴C. Carbon is one of the most prevalent elements in all biological macromolecules, and glucose is the only carbon source available. The cells must therefore use carbon atoms from the labeled glucose to build every type of macromolecule.
item.verification_python:
from fractions import Fraction
A = {'protein': 97, 'nucleic': 2, 'phospholipid': 1}
B = {'protein': 4, 'nucleic': 78, 'phospholipid': 18}
assert sum(A.values()) == 100
assert sum(B.values()) == 100
assert max(A, key=A.get) == 'protein'
total = 50000
phos = Fraction(B['phospholipid'], 100) * total
assert phos == 9000
assert abs(0.18 * total - 9000) < 1e-9
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.stimulus:
A student investigates which elements from the environment bacteria use to build their macromolecules. Two cultures of E. coli are grown in a liquid medium that contains glucose as the only carbon source plus all required mineral salts.

Culture 1: the sulfate (SO₄²⁻) in the medium contains radioactive sulfur-35 (³⁵S).
Culture 2: the phosphate (PO₄³⁻) in the medium contains radioactive phosphorus-32 (³²P).

After several generations, the cells from each culture are collected, and their molecules are separated into four fractions: protein, nucleic acid (DNA and RNA), lipid, and carbohydrate (stored polysaccharide). The radioactivity of each fraction is measured in counts per minute (cpm). Readings of about 60 cpm or less are considered background radiation (no meaningful label).

Radioactivity in each fraction (cpm)
Fraction | Culture 1 (³⁵S) | Culture 2 (³²P)
Protein | 5200 | 60
Nucleic acid | 50 | 8400
Lipid | 45 | 1500
Carbohydrate | 40 | 40
Total | 5335 | 10000
item.model_answer:
(a) Most of the ³⁵S was in the protein fraction (5200 cpm, compared with background levels of 40 to 50 cpm in the other fractions). Sulfur is used to build proteins because it is part of the R groups of some amino acids, so the bacteria used the radioactive sulfate to make sulfur-containing amino acids that were linked into proteins.

(b) The nucleic acid fraction was labeled because each nucleotide in DNA and RNA contains a phosphate group, and these phosphates form the sugar-phosphate backbone, so the bacteria built the ³²P into their nucleic acids. The lipid fraction was labeled because phospholipids, the lipids that form the cell membrane bilayer, contain a phosphate group. The carbohydrate fraction stayed at background because polysaccharides are made only of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

(c) Percentage in nucleic acid = (8400 cpm ÷ 10000 cpm) × 100 = 84%.

(d) The population without phosphate will grow much less than Culture 2, and growth will slow or stop. Phosphorus is required to build nucleotides for new DNA and RNA and to build phospholipids for new membranes. Without a phosphorus source from the environment, the cells cannot replicate their DNA or make the membranes needed to form new cells, so cell division will stop.

assert sum(c2.values()) == 10000

pct = Fraction(c2['nucleic'], sum(c2.values()))*100
assert pct == 84
assert Fraction(c2['nucleic'], sum(c2.values())) == Fraction(84,100)
for k in ['nucleic','lipid','carb']:
    assert c1[k] <= 60
assert c2['protein'] <= 60 and c2['carb'] <= 60
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

item.title: Tracing Sulfur and Phosphorus into Bacterial Macromolecules
item.stimulus:
Students investigated which elements bacteria use to build different macromolecules. They grew two cultures of the same bacterial species in identical growth media. In each medium, all required nutrients were supplied, but one element was supplied only in a radioactive form.

Culture A: the only sulfur source was sulfate containing radioactive sulfur-35 (35S).
Culture B: the only phosphorus source was phosphate containing radioactive phosphorus-32 (32P).

After several hours of growth, the cells from each culture were washed and broken open. Their contents were separated into four macromolecule fractions. The radioactivity of each fraction was measured in counts per minute (cpm). Values of about 300 cpm or less are considered background, meaning no meaningful amount of the label was built into that fraction.

Fraction | Culture A (35S), cpm | Culture B (32P), cpm
Protein | 9,800 | 300
Nucleic acid (DNA and RNA) | 150 | 7,200
Phospholipid | 120 | 2,400
Carbohydrate | 90 | 100
item.model_answer:
(a) The protein fraction incorporated the 35S label (9,800 cpm, far above the 300 cpm background). Sulfur is an element used to build proteins; it is found in the R groups of certain amino acids. Nucleic acids, phospholipids, and carbohydrates do not contain sulfur, so they stayed at background.

(b) Total 32P in Culture B = 300 + 7,200 + 2,400 + 100 = 10,000 cpm. Percentage in nucleic acid = 7,200 / 10,000 × 100 = 72%.

(c) Carbohydrates are built only from carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. They contain no sulfur and no phosphorus, so neither 35S nor 32P could be built into them, and the carbohydrate fraction stayed at background (90 and 100 cpm) in both cultures.

(d) Prediction: The bacteria will be unable to make new DNA and new phospholipids for membranes, so their growth and cell division will slow and stop. Justification: Phosphorus is a required component of nucleic acids, since every nucleotide includes a phosphate group, and of phospholipids, which have a phosphate-containing head. Cells cannot make elements; the atoms needed to build new molecules must come from the environment. Without a phosphorus source, these molecules cannot be assembled, which Culture B confirms because 32P appeared mainly in the nucleic acid and phospholipid fractions.

item.title: Tracing Sulfur and Phosphorus Isotopes into Macromolecules
item.stimulus:
Researchers grew two cultures of the bacterium Escherichia coli for several generations in a medium containing glucose and mineral salts. Culture 1 received sulfate containing radioactive sulfur (³⁵S) as its only sulfur source. Culture 2 received phosphate containing radioactive phosphorus (³²P) as its only phosphorus source. The cells were then collected and separated into four macromolecule fractions, and the radioactivity in each fraction was measured in counts per minute (cpm). Values of 25 cpm or less are considered background.

Fraction | Culture 1 (³⁵S) cpm | Culture 2 (³²P) cpm
Proteins | 1,940 | 15
Nucleic acids | 20 | 1,620
Lipids | 25 | 360
Carbohydrates | 15 | 5
Total | 2,000 | 2,000
item.model_answer:
(a) Proteins contain most of the ³⁵S (1,940 of 2,000 cpm, about 97%). Sulfur is a component of some amino acids, in their R groups, so when the cells build proteins from amino acids made using the sulfate, the labeled sulfur becomes part of the proteins.

(b) 1,620 cpm ÷ 2,000 cpm × 100 = 81% of the ³²P is in the nucleic acid fraction.

(c) Phosphorus is used to build phospholipids, a type of lipid that has a phosphate group, so the ³²P was incorporated into the lipid fraction of Culture 2 (360 cpm). Lipids do not contain sulfur, so ³⁵S was not built into lipids, and the lipid fraction in Culture 1 stayed at background (25 cpm).

(d) The rate of synthesis of new nucleic acids and new phospholipids will decrease, and eventually stop, compared with Culture 2. Cells must take in atoms from the environment to build new molecules. Phosphorus is a required part of every nucleotide in DNA and RNA and of phospholipids, so with no phosphorus available the cells cannot build these molecules.

item.title: Tracing Labeled Sulfur and Phosphorus into Macromolecules
item.stimulus:
Researchers grew two cultures of the same bacterium. Each culture's food source contained one radioactively labeled element. Cells use a radioactive form of an element in the same way as the ordinary form.

Culture 1: sulfur-35 (³⁵S)
Culture 2: phosphorus-32 (³²P)

After several generations, the cells from each culture were broken open and their molecules were separated into four fractions: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids. The radioactivity of each fraction was measured in counts per minute (cpm). Readings below 100 cpm are background and show that the label was not incorporated.

Fraction | Culture 1 (³⁵S), cpm | Culture 2 (³²P), cpm
Carbohydrates | 30 | 40
Lipids | 25 | 2100
Proteins | 8800 | 35
Nucleic acids | 20 | 6400

parts.prompt: Explain why the ³⁵S in Culture 1 was incorporated into the protein fraction.

criteria.text: Explains that sulfur is an element used in building proteins, so the cells built ³⁵S into the proteins they made.
criteria.evidence: Response states that sulfur is used to build proteins (is part of proteins) and connects this to the label appearing in the protein fraction.
criteria.fix: Memorize the element linked to each macromolecule: sulfur is used in building proteins, so a sulfur label marks protein.

parts.prompt: In Culture 2, ³²P was incorporated into two different fractions. Explain why each of these two fractions became labeled.

criteria.text: Explains that phosphorus is used in building nucleic acids, so ³²P was incorporated into the nucleic acid fraction (6400 cpm).
criteria.evidence: Response links the labeled nucleic acid fraction to phosphorus being an element used to build nucleic acids.
criteria.fix: Recall phosphorus is used in building nucleic acids; check that fraction first when a phosphorus label is used.

criteria.text: Explains that phosphorus is used in building phospholipids, a type of lipid, so ³²P was incorporated into the lipid fraction (2100 cpm).
criteria.evidence: Response links the labeled lipid fraction to phosphorus being an element used to build phospholipids.
criteria.fix: Recall phosphorus also builds phospholipids, which are lipids; a phosphorus label therefore appears in the lipid fraction too.

parts.prompt: Cellulose is a carbohydrate. A researcher grows cotton plants with ³²P in their water and then purifies cellulose from the cotton fibers. Predict whether the purified cellulose will contain ³²P, and justify your prediction.

criteria.evidence: Response states the cellulose will not be labeled with ³²P.
criteria.fix: Decide whether the molecule class contains the labeled element; if not, predict no label in the purified molecule.

criteria.text: Justifies the prediction: carbohydrates such as cellulose are built from carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen and do not contain phosphorus.
criteria.evidence: Response states that carbohydrates are made of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen (no phosphorus), so phosphorus is not built into cellulose.
criteria.fix: Justify with elemental composition: carbohydrates are built of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen only, so they lack phosphorus.

item.model_answer:
(a) Sulfur is one of the elements used in building proteins. As the bacteria made new proteins, they used the ³⁵S from their food, so the label appeared in the protein fraction (8800 cpm), while the other fractions stayed at background.

(b) Phosphorus is used in building nucleic acids, so the cells built ³²P into their nucleic acids, labeling the nucleic acid fraction (6400 cpm).
Phosphorus is also used in building phospholipids, which are a type of lipid, so ³²P was built into phospholipids and the lipid fraction was labeled (2100 cpm).

(c) The purified cellulose will not contain ³²P. Cellulose is a carbohydrate, and carbohydrates are built from carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen; they do not contain phosphorus. This matches the data: the carbohydrate fraction in Culture 2 stayed at background (40 cpm).
